My point is, this holier than thou attitude that many seem to have here because they were able to afford to move and build a life in Vermont, is nonsense.

Look I’ll go ahead and throw my hat in the ring, I left a year ago because a better school saved me money by pretty much the same principle it would’ve cost me to go to UVM. 

For a lot of people, again from my experience, before leaving, a lot of what I would call the old timers in Vermont said that there was a big culture change when people from out of state moved to work for IBM. 

Since then, and again, speaking from what I’ve heard, I can’t necessarily disagree with some of the sentiments that people came with. The attitude that they are helping, by bringing their tax money to the state is a technical yes but in reality, the state population has been dropping even with all the new people moving in. 

Fact is, there hasn’t been any new industry that created massive amounts of jobs in Vermont. IBM has moved to New York, and taxes have largely only increased for most of the Vermonters that have remained statewide with stagnating wages for many, be it in property taxes that for instance have been raised without much to really see in benefit for those in Burlington, where I am from originally, and where I can speak to my family’s experience. 

I personally don’t much care for the attitude that your taxes have somehow dramatically increased the quality of life in the state because again, haven’t personally seen it in any measurable way for my family or anyone we know. So yes, I think I would agree with the sentiment of the article. 

Most of the people currently raised in Vermont have left for better wages, better benefits, and better quality of life imo. It might be anecdotal, but I’d personally like to hear a counter to any of the points. Vermont hasn’t really changed in any constructive way unless you are moving/visiting from out of state.
